source.title: Twelve weeks of supervised resistance training and fall risk in community-dwelling adults aged 65 to 84: a randomised controlled trial
source.abstract: Falls are the leading cause of injury-related hospital admission in older adults. We randomised 288 community-dwelling adults aged 65 to 84 who had experienced at least one fall in the previous year to either twelve weeks of supervised resistance training twice weekly at a local community centre, or to a control group receiving a printed falls-prevention leaflet. Training sessions lasted 45 minutes and used adjustable ankle weights and resistance bands. Participants recorded falls in a monthly diary for twelve months after the end of the programme. The training group reported 27% fewer falls over the follow-up year (incidence rate ratio 0.73, 95% CI 0.58 to 0.92). Lower-limb strength measured by the 30-second chair-stand test improved by 2.4 repetitions in the training group and by 0.3 in the control group. Adherence was 81%. Nine participants withdrew because of joint pain. The trial was open-label and fall reporting relied on self-report.
source.tldr: Twice-weekly resistance training for twelve weeks reduced falls by 27% over the following year in adults aged 65 to 84.
